newsitem.title: USA: Arraignment set for Friday in Army harassment case.
newsitem.headline: Arraignment set for Friday in Army harassment case.

text.p: Three U.S. Army trainers charged in a rape and sexual harassment scandal at the army's Aberdeen Proving Ground are to be arraigned here Friday, military authorities announced on Thursday.

The three men -- two drill instructors and a company commander -- have been charged in connection with allegations of coerced sex and harrassment involving at least 17 women at the Army Ordnance and Doctrine Command's training facility.
The accused will be arraigned before a military judge. They are expected to enter a plea, and a trial date, probably for early next year, will be set, base spokesman Gary Holloway said.

The accusations have sparked widening investigations into harassment in the military, and an order by outgoing Defence Secretary William Perry to drive home a message of "zero tolerance" for sexual harrassment in the armed services.

An additional 15 people have been suspended from their duties at the Aberdeen base pending results of the continuing probe. Two others were fined in connection with the probe, with the punishments included in their military records.
--- Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson, who has been jailed on charges of rape, sodomy, adultery, obstruction of justice and fraternisation with recruits.
-- Capt. Derrick Robertson, charged with rape, adultery, fraternisation and conduct unbecoming an officer. Robertson has been relieved of duty pending investigation.
-- Staff Sgt. Nathanial Beach, charged with disobeying an order, fraternisation and obstruction of justice.
Neither Robertson nor Beach were in custody, Holloway said.
Possible sentences for a rape conviction range from a letter of reprimand to life in prison, at the discretion of the military court.
